title: Quantitative analysis of DNA-GATA1 binding alterations linked to hematopoietic disorders
authors: Boglarka Zambo; Bastien Morlet; Luc Negroni; Orsolya Mózner; Balázs Sarkadi; Gilles Travé; Gergo Gogl
one_liner_zh: 该文用原生holdup实验定量分析GATA1突变对DNA结合亲和力的影响，虽聚焦TF-DNA互作但方法为湿实验定量，缺乏AI或物理模拟建模，故为中档匹配。
abstract: GATA1 is a crucial transcription factor involved in hematopoiesis, and mutations in this gene are linked to severe hematological disorders, including anemia, thrombocytopenia, Down-syndrome related transient abnormal myelopoiesis (DS-TAM) and acute megakaryocytic leukemia (DS- AMKL). Despite significant clinical interest in the molecular level characterization of GATA1 mutations, a comprehensive understanding of their impact on DNA binding is limited. Efforts to conduct detailed studies on full-length recombinant GATA1 have faced significant technical challenges, while alternative approaches are limited by low throughput or qualitative nature. Here, we introduce a native holdup (nHU) assay designed to systematically quantify DNA-protein interactions and suitable for studying the impact of transcription factor mutations on DNA-binding affinity. First, we demonstrate, using the erythroid-specific ATP2B4 promoter as a model, that nHU can capture sequence-specific interactions and detect even subtle differences in DNA binding affinities of GATA1. Then, we quantitatively characterize the impact of pathological mutations on DNA binding affinities in the context of full-length human GATA1. Our findings reveal that the short isoform, lacking the N-terminal transactivation domain (N-TAD), binds to DNA with increased affinity, while the R307C mutation reduces binding to the ATP2B4 erythroid promoter. In harmony with these observations, GATA1s exhibits increased functional activity, while the R307C mutation results in decreased activity. This study demonstrates the power of the nHU assay for studying DNA interactions of transcription factor variants and providing insight into the molecular mechanism of related diseases.
abstract_zh: GATA1是参与造血过程的关键转录因子，该基因的突变与严重血液疾病相关，包括贫血、血小板减少症、唐氏综合征相关的短暂异常骨髓增生（DS-TAM）和急性巨核细胞白血病（DS-AMKL）。尽管在分子水平上表征GATA1突变具有重要的临床意义，但对其对DNA结合影响的全面理解仍有限。对全长重组GATA1进行详细研究的努力面临重大技术挑战，而替代方法则受限于低通量或定性性质。在此，我们引入一种天然滞留（nHU）测定法，旨在系统量化DNA-蛋白质相互作用，并适用于研究转录因子突变对DNA结合亲和力的影响。首先，我们以红细胞特异性ATP2B4启动子为模型，证明nHU能够捕获序列特异性相互作用，并检测GATA1 DNA结合亲和力的细微差异。随后，我们在全长人GATA1背景下定量表征病理突变对DNA结合亲和力的影响。我们的发现揭示，缺乏N端反式激活结构域（N-TAD）的短异构体以更高亲和力结合DNA，而R307C突变则降低对ATP2B4红细胞启动子的结合。与这些观察一致，GATA1s表现出增强的功能活性，而R307C突变导致活性降低。本研究展示了nHU测定法在研究转录因子变体DNA相互作用及提供相关疾病分子机制见解方面的强大能力。
